Their 1998 debut album gave them 'Definition', 'Brown Skin Lady' and 'Respiration', the last a nocturnal city portrait shared with Common. Both men then pursued solo careers, and for more than two decades the duo existed mainly as a promise, surfacing on singles and compilations until a second album finally appeared in 2022. That first record remains a touchstone for anyone arguing that conscious rap could also be a pleasure.

mosdef.blurb: Conscious Brooklyn MC turned singer and actor.
mosdef.bio: Mos Def, born in 1973 and later known as Yasiin Bey, is an American MC, singer and actor, and one of the defining voices of conscious hip hop. He drew attention first as half of Black Star, before 'Black on Both Sides' in 1999 established him alone, a record wide enough to hold the wry storytelling of 'Ms. Fat Booty', the cold arithmetic of 'Mathematics' and the yearning, half-sung 'Umi Says'. His writing turns on wordplay and on plain speech about police violence, American exceptionalism and the position of Black people in the United States. He has recorded with Common and Immortal Technique, and shared a generation and a sensibility with MF DOOM. Acting drew him steadily away from records, but that late-nineties run still sets the standard for what conscious rap can sound like.

talibkweli.blurb: Brooklyn MC of dense, restless political lyricism.
talibkweli.bio: Talib Kweli, born in 1975, is an American MC from Brooklyn who formed Black Star with Mos Def in 1997. Their single 'Definition' reached the Billboard Hot 100 the following year and led the way for a debut album that charted too, an unlikely commercial result for rap this dense and this unwilling to simplify itself. 'Respiration', made with Common, showed the other side of him: patient, observational, alive to the texture of a city at night. He went solo soon after, and in 2002 'Get By', produced by Kanye West, became the closest thing he has had to a hit without a single softened line. An entrepreneur and activist as well as a rapper, he reunited with Mos Def for a second Black Star album in 2022.

e40.blurb: Bay Area slang inventor and independent hustler.
e40.bio: E-40, born Earl Stevens in 1967, is an American MC from the San Francisco Bay Area and one of rap's great independent operators. He came up in the group the Click and founded his own label, Sick Wid It Records, releasing at a pace few match, more than two dozen albums and counting. His gift is language: a rubbery invented slang delivered in sudden bursts and drawls that has seeded phrases across the whole of hip hop. 'In a Major Way' in 1995 carried him out of the underground, with 'Sprinkle Me' alongside Suga-T, and in 2006 'Tell Me When to Go', produced by Lil Jon, made him the voice of hyphy, the Bay's own hyperactive dance movement. He has recorded with Too $hort and 2Pac, and Saweetie is among the younger Bay artists raised on him.

eminem.blurb: Detroit MC of ferocious technique and controversy.
eminem.bio: Eminem, born Marshall Mathers in 1972, is an American MC whose technique, all internal rhyme, elastic flow and sheer rate of syllables, reset expectations of what a rapper could fit inside a bar. Dr. Dre found him, produced him and vouched for him, and the records that followed made him the most argued-over figure in music: 'The Real Slim Shady' in 2000 as gleeful provocation, 'Stan' the same year as a chilling piece of storytelling about a fan, and 'Lose Yourself' in 2002, written for the film '8 Mile' and an Academy Award winner. He is widely credited with carrying hip hop into middle America and with making a white rapper's success possible without novelty. He came up with the group D12 and his friend Proof, and later signed and mentored 50 Cent.

50cent.blurb: Queens MC turned relentless commercial mogul.
50cent.bio: 50 Cent, born Curtis Jackson in Queens in 1975, is an American MC and businessman whose career reads as a long lesson in leverage. Jam Master Jay took him on early. A debut album for Columbia was shelved after he was shot nine times in 2000 and dropped by the label, and he rebuilt himself through mixtapes until 'Guess Who's Back?' reached Eminem, who signed him to Shady Records with Dr. Dre alongside. What followed in 2003 was total: 'In da Club', 'P.I.M.P.' and 'Many Men (Wish Death)', menace and melody delivered in the same unbothered drawl. He founded the crew G-Unit and turned rivalry into marketing, feuding publicly with The Game and with Rick Ross. He later mentored Pop Smoke and moved steadily into television and business, where the same instinct for scale has served him well.

gunit.blurb: 50 Cent's crew at its commercial peak.
gunit.bio: G-Unit were an American group in hip hop, put together by 50 Cent with his longtime friends Tony Yayo and Lloyd Banks, later joined by The Game. They built their following the hard way first, flooding the streets with self-released mixtapes until the demand was impossible to ignore, then converted it wholesale with 'Beg for Mercy' in 2003, an album that sold more than two million copies in the United States. 'Stunt 101' introduced them, 'Poppin' Them Thangs' hardened the picture, and 'Wanna Get to Know You' with Joe softened it enough for radio. As much a brand as a band, the crew turned group membership into a launchpad for solo careers and made the unit itself the era's model for how a rapper builds an empire around himself.

kanye.blurb: Producer turned MC who reshaped rap's possibilities.
kanye.bio: Kanye West, born in 1977, is an American producer and MC who changed what a rapper was allowed to be. He made his name behind the desk, building tracks for Jay-Z and for Common out of sped-up soul samples, with Just Blaze working the same seam nearby and the example of J Dilla behind them both. As a performer he broke through with 'Through the Wire' in 2003, followed by 'Jesus Walks', a gospel-driven single nobody expected to work on radio, and 'Stronger' in 2007, which pulled electronic music into the mainstream of rap. His restless shifts of style opened a door for rappers with no interest in gangsta convention, among them Kid Cudi, Pusha T and Big Sean, whom he signed and mentored. A polarising public figure, his effect on the music is not in dispute.

lilwayne.blurb: New Orleans MC who rapped like nobody else.
lilwayne.bio: Lil Wayne, born Dwayne Carter in New Orleans in 1982, is an American MC who signed to Cash Money Records at eleven after Birdman took him under his wing, and grew up in public as the label's flagship artist. He ran with Juvenile in the Cash Money years before remaking himself in the 2000s as rap's most prolific and least predictable writer, a rasping voice piling metaphor on metaphor at a pace that made his mixtapes feel more urgent than most albums. 'Go DJ' in 2004 pointed the way; 'A Milli' and 'Lollipop', both from 2008, showed his two poles, one all rhyme and no chorus, the other sung through Auto-Tune. He mentored Drake and Nicki Minaj, recorded with Trina, and left fingerprints on Young Thug and YoungBoy Never Broke Again.

ti.blurb: Atlanta MC who helped invent trap.
ti.bio: T.I., born Clifford Harris in Atlanta in 1980, is an American MC credited alongside Jeezy and Gucci Mane with founding trap, the subgenre that took its name and its subject from the corners his early records described. A first album for an Arista imprint in 2001 went nowhere and he parted with the label, then signed to Atlantic and co-founded his own Grand Hustle imprint in 2003. From there the run was long: 'Bring Em Out' in 2004, and in 2008 'Whatever You Like' and 'Live Your Life' with Rihanna, hits that carried a southern accent into the centre of American pop. He has worked with Ludacris, Jeezy and Lil Jon, fellow architects of his city's takeover, and younger Atlanta rappers such as Latto grew up inside the template he set.

ludacris.blurb: Atlanta MC with cartoon energy and comic timing.
ludacris.bio: Ludacris, born Christopher Bridges in Illinois in 1977, is an American MC who found his voice after moving to Atlanta, first through a brief spell as a DJ and then as a rapper with a comic's timing and a cartoonist's sense of scale. He founded his own label, Disturbing tha Peace, and released 'Incognegro' independently in 1999; when its single reached the charts, Def Jam picked the record up and reissued it as 'Back for the First Time' in 2000. What followed was a decade of hits built on elastic, exaggerated delivery: 'Move Bitch' in 2001, the number one 'Stand Up' in 2003, 'Get Back' the year after. He has recorded with T.I., ran with 2 Chainz, and shared the crossover moment with Nelly. Acting later widened his audience without much changing the persona.

nelly.blurb: St. Louis MC who made rap sing.
nelly.bio: Nelly, born Cornell Haynes in 1974, is an American MC who grew up in St. Louis and started out in 1993 with the local group St. Lunatics. Signing to Universal as a solo act in 1999, he arrived with 'Country Grammar' in 2000, a debut that went to number one and eventually to diamond certification, carried by a sing-song delivery pitched halfway between rapping and a playground chant, and making the Midwest audible in a business run from the coasts. 'Nellyville' in 2002 went further, giving him two number one singles in 'Hot in Herre' and 'Dilemma' with Kelly Rowland. The knack was melody: hooks that lodged instantly and left the door open for every rapper who wanted to sing. He shared that crossover decade with Ludacris.

theneptunes.blurb: Virginia production duo who stripped pop bare.
theneptunes.bio: The Neptunes were an American production duo, Chad Hugo and Pharrell Williams, who came together in Virginia Beach in 1992. Their sound was built on subtraction: a handful of clipped synth stabs, hard empty space, and drums that sounded programmed on a toy, an approach so distinctive that for a stretch of the early 2000s it seemed to play from every radio at once. 'Grindin' for Clipse in 2002 reduced a hit to little more than a beat knocked out on a lunch table, while 'Hot in Herre' for Nelly that same year and 'Drop It Like It's Hot' for Snoop Dogg in 2004 showed how far the minimalism could travel. Williams sang the hooks and appeared in the videos while Hugo stayed behind the desk. Between them they set the rhythmic grammar of a decade of pop.

pharrell.blurb: Producer, singer and pop's perennial cool hand.
pharrell.bio: Pharrell Williams, born in 1973, is an American producer, singer and rapper who became one of the most influential figures in modern pop while barely raising his voice. He established the Neptunes with Chad Hugo in 1992, a partnership that put fifteen productions into the top ten and four of them at number one, and in 1999 he formed the band N.E.R.D with Shay Haley, singing lead on rowdier, rock-leaning records such as 'Lapdance'. Stepping out front, he turned 'Frontin' with Jay-Z in 2003 into a falsetto hit, and a decade later 'Happy', written for an animated film, became one of the most ubiquitous songs of its era. His fingerprints, the light touch and the unhurried cool, are all over Tyler, the Creator and everyone who took him as proof a producer could be a star.

clipse.blurb: Virginia Beach brothers, cold and precise.
clipse.bio: Clipse are a Virginia Beach hip hop duo, the American brothers Pusha T and Malice, who later took the name No Malice. Formed in the early nineties, they wrote about the drug trade with a coldness and a precision that set them apart from everyone working the same material, all detail and dry wit in place of swagger. The Neptunes produced them, and 'Grindin' in 2002 became their breakout on the strength of a beat so spare it sounded like knuckles on a lunch table. 'Hell Hath No Fury' in 2006, carrying 'Mr. Me Too' alongside Pharrell, is the record most often named as their best. They did as much as anyone to establish Virginia as a southern stronghold, and returned in 2025 with 'Chains & Whips', trading verses with Kendrick Lamar.

pushat.blurb: Coke rap's sharpest and most quotable technician.
pushat.bio: Pusha T, born Terrence Thornton in 1977, is an American MC who came up as one half of Clipse with his older brother Malice. Pharrell Williams discovered the duo and signed them to his Star Trak label in 2001, and across 'Lord Willin', 'Hell Hath No Fury' and 'Til the Casket Drops' they turned drug-trade narrative into something closer to precision engineering. Solo, he sharpened further: 'Nosetalgia' in 2013 set him beside Kendrick Lamar, 'Numbers on the Boards' stripped the form back to a sneer and a drum, and 'If You Know You Know', produced by Kanye West in 2018, opened the most acclaimed record of his career. He has worked closely with West for years, and his long public feud with Drake produced some of the most quoted verses of the decade.

jeezy.blurb: Georgia trap pioneer with a hustler's growl.
jeezy.bio: Jeezy, born in 1977, is an American MC whose gravelled, motivational delivery helped carry trap music out of Georgia and into the mainstream. After a run of independent releases at the start of the 2000s he signed to Def Jam and broke through in 2005 with 'Let's Get It: Thug Motivation 101', a debut that hardened street reportage into anthems. 'Soul Survivor', cut with Akon that same year, remains his signature; 'Go Crazy' drew a Jay-Z verse on its remix, and 'Put On' brought Kanye West aboard in 2008. He shares credit with T.I. and Gucci Mane, both Georgia rappers, for dragging trap out of the region and into the pop charts, though his rivalry with Gucci Mane became one of the South's most bitter. A frequent collaborator with Rick Ross, he built a parallel career as a music executive and entrepreneur.

guccimane.blurb: Atlanta trap godfather and mixtape machine.
guccimane.bio: Gucci Mane, born in 1980, is an American MC and music executive who, together with the Atlanta rappers T.I. and Jeezy, is credited with carrying trap into the 2000s mainstream. His 2005 debut 'Trap House' arrived on the independent Big Cat label, and the following year 'Freaky Gurl', built on an interpolation of Rick James, gave him his first national hit. A move to Atlantic followed for 'Back to the Trap House', but it was his relentless mixtape output that made him first a local institution and then a national one. 'Wasted', cut with Plies, and 'Lemonade' catch the run at its peak in 2009. He shares an influence line with Three 6 Mafia and made records with Lil Jon and Soulja Boy, while his feud with Jeezy shadowed the decade. As a mentor to Future, Young Thug and Migos, he seeded the trap generation that followed.

liljon.blurb: Crunk architect who made clubs shout.
liljon.bio: Lil Jon, born in 1971, is an American producer, MC and DJ, and the figure most responsible for taking crunk out of the clubs and onto national radio. As frontman of Lil Jon and the East Side Boyz he released five albums, his roared ad-libs riding beats built for maximum room-shaking impact. 'Get Low', cut with the Ying Yang Twins in 2002, became the template; two years later his production on Usher's 'Yeah!' turned the sound into a pop phenomenon, and 'Snap Yo Fingers' followed in 2006 with E-40 and Sean Paul aboard. He worked with T.I., Gucci Mane and T-Pain, and his lineage runs back through Three 6 Mafia. Beyond the booth he built a career as a music executive and entrepreneur. Few producers of the decade left a more instantly recognisable signature on the sound of the American club.

tpain.blurb: Auto-Tune pioneer who reshaped rap singing.
tpain.bio: T-Pain, born in 1985, is an American vocalist, rapper, songwriter and producer who made Auto-Tune an instrument rather than a repair tool. Pushing the pitch-correction software to extreme settings, he built a gleaming, electronic vocal style and married it to R&B and hip hop songwriting, defining the rap-singing that ran through the second half of the 2000s. 'I'm Sprung' announced him in 2005, and by 2007 'Buy U a Drank (Shawty Snappin')', made with Yung Joc, and 'Bartender' with Akon had put his voice on every radio station in the country. He worked closely with Lil Jon, and a direct line runs from his experiments to Kanye West and the melodic rappers who followed. Widely imitated and often parodied in his own time, he is now credited as the craftsman who opened rap up to unashamed singing.

rickross.blurb: Southern boss with a booming, cinematic voice.
rickross.bio: Rick Ross, born in 1976, is an American MC and music executive whose booming voice and vivid, luxurious imagery turned a rags-to-riches narrative into a whole aesthetic. His 2006 breakthrough 'Hustlin'' set the template, and by the turn of the decade 'B.M.F. (Blowin' Money Fast)' with Styles P and 'Aston Martin Music', featuring Drake and Chrisette Michele, had widened the boss persona into something close to widescreen soul. As a mogul he signed Wale and Meek Mill, giving both a national platform, and he kept company with Sean 'Diddy' Combs as a fellow executive. He recorded with Jeezy and Trina, and his long feud with 50 Cent ran through the same years. Ross remains one of Southern rap's most durable businessmen as well as one of its most quotable voices, still built around that unmistakable low rumble.

camron.blurb: East Coast stylist and Diplomats ringleader.
camron.bio: Cam'ron, born in 1976, is an American MC who first recorded as Killa Cam in the early 1990s and grew into one of East Coast rap's most idiosyncratic stylists. Signed to Untertainment through Epic, he released 'Confessions of Fire' in 1998 and 'S.D.E.' in 2000 before moving to Roc-A-Fella, where 'Come Home with Me' arrived in 2002 carrying 'Oh Boy' and 'Hey Ma', both cut with Juelz Santana and both enormous hits. 'Purple Haze' followed in 2004, as did 'Down and Out' with Kanye West. He was the central figure of The Diplomats, the crew whose loose, taunting delivery became a dialect of its own. His public falling-out with Jay-Z defined a chapter of Roc-A-Fella history. Cam'ron remains a byword for charisma winning out over convention.

dipset.blurb: Harlem collective that ruled 2000s New York.
dipset.bio: The Diplomats came together in Harlem during the summer of 1997 around the childhood friendship of Cam'ron and Jim Jones, with Freekey Zekey completing the original line-up and Juelz Santana joining in 1999. Better known as Dipset, the American collective turned neighbourhood loyalty into a brand, and their loose, taunting delivery and unbothered swagger became one of the defining New York sounds of the early 2000s. The 2003 run of 'Dipset Anthem', cut with Juelz Santana, alongside 'I Really Mean It' and 'Built This City', catches the crew at full strength, trading verses over soul samples pitched high and hard. Built around Cam'ron, the collective operated as much as a movement as a group, sweeping in rappers, hangers-on and a whole style of dress. Their mark on the attitude of New York rap long outlasted their peak.

thegame.blurb: Compton MC who revived West Coast rap.
thegame.bio: The Game, born in 1979, is an American MC from Compton whose arrival returned West Coast rap to the centre of the map. He built early mixtapes alongside JT the Bigga Figga, another West Coast rapper, and put out 'Untold Story' independently in 2004 before Dr. Dre discovered him and signed him to Aftermath. Dre's production and G-Unit membership framed his 2005 major-label debut 'The Documentary', which reached the top of the Billboard 200, went double platinum and earned two Grammy nominations for 'Hate It or Love It', the 50 Cent duet that remains his signature. 'How We Do' had preceded it and 'Dreams' followed, and the sequel 'Doctor's Advocate' repeated the chart feat in 2006. His split from 50 Cent became one of rap's most public feuds. Encyclopaedic in his references, he made a career of naming his lineage.

fabolous.blurb: Brooklyn punchline artist with radio instincts.
fabolous.bio: Fabolous, born in 1977 and raised in Brooklyn, is an American MC who turned relaxed punchline rap into a decade of radio staples. His break came on DJ Clue's Hot 97 show, where a live guest spot led to a deal with Clue's Desert Storm label, in partnership with Elektra Records. His 2001 debut 'Ghetto Fabolous' produced 'Can't Deny It', built around a Nate Dogg hook, and a more commercially minded second album, 'Street Dreams', followed in 2003, sending both 'Can't Let You Go' and 'Into You', his duet with Tamia, to No.4 on the Billboard Hot 100. 'Breathe' arrived the next year. A frequent partner of Jadakiss, he kept a steady presence in New York rap long after the era that made him. His gift was the conversational boast, delivered as though he were barely trying.

souljaboy.blurb: Internet-native teenager who cracked the charts.
souljaboy.bio: Soulja Boy, born in 1990, is an American MC and record producer who showed a generation that a bedroom, a laptop and a website could do the work of a record label. He self-released 'Crank That (Soulja Boy)' in 2007, and the track, complete with its own dance, spent seven non-consecutive weeks at the top of the Billboard Hot 100 before Collipark Music and Interscope picked it up. 'Soulja Girl' followed, then the debut album 'Souljaboytellem.com', which reached number four despite hostile reviews and spawned 'Yahhh!'. 'Kiss Me Thru the Phone', made with Sammie, and 'Turn My Swag On' extended the run through 2008. He recorded with Gucci Mane and stayed close to the snap and Southern rap scenes that raised him. Dismissed at the time as a novelty, he is now read as the first rapper to build a career natively online.

kidcudi.blurb: Melancholy hummer who opened rap's emotional lane.
kidcudi.bio: Kid Cudi, born in 1984, is an American MC, singer and producer who moved from Cleveland to New York in pursuit of a career and found one almost by accident. He posted the single Day 'n' Nite to his MySpace page, where it spread online and drew him to the producers Plain Pat and Emile Haynie for the 2008 mixtape 'A Kid Named Cudi'. Kanye West heard it and signed him to GOOD Music by the end of that year, becoming first a mentor and then a crewmate, with the two sharing 'Erase Me' in 2010. 'Pursuit of Happiness', made with MGMT and Ratatat in 2009, remains his defining statement: hummed, hazy and openly depressive at a moment when rap admitted to neither. That candour ran straight into Travis Scott and Childish Gambino, both of whom carry his imprint.

wale.blurb: DC rapper who carried go-go into hits.
wale.bio: Wale, born in 1984, is an American MC who built his name on the go-go rhythms of the Washington DC region before turning them into national records. Local recognition came with 'Dig Dug' in 2006 and a string of follow-ups around Germantown, Maryland, and in 2007 the English DJ and producer Mark Ronson signed him to Allido, which the following year tied up with Interscope for US$1.3 million once three labels had bid against each other. His mixtapes made him a fixture of the blog era and of MTV coverage. He guested on Waka Flocka Flame's 'No Hands' with Roscoe Dash in 2010, then found his own signature with 'Lotus Flower Bomb', cut with Miguel in 2011, and 'Bad' with Tiara Thomas two years later. Rick Ross later signed him, giving his wordy, romantic style a Southern platform it had not had before.

jdilla.blurb: Detroit producer whose drums bent time.
jdilla.bio: J Dilla, born in 1974, was an American producer, rapper and composer whose off-kilter, hand-played drum programming changed how a generation heard rhythm. He came up in Detroit's mid-1990s underground as a member of Slum Village, produced the Pharcyde album 'Labcabincalifornia', and helped found the Soulquarians, the collective around Questlove that reshaped soul and rap at the turn of the century. He worked with A Tribe Called Quest, produced for Common, and joined Madlib as the duo Jaylib for 'Champion Sound'. 'Fall in Love', made with Slum Village in 2000, shows his ear for a slurred, romantic loop; 'Workinonit' and 'Won't Do' come from the final year of a life cut short in 2006, the album 'Donuts' arriving three days before his death. Kanye West, Blu and Kota the Friend all trace lines back to him.

mfdoom.blurb: Masked villain of underground rap wordplay.
mfdoom.bio: MF DOOM, born in 1971 and both British and American, was a rapper, songwriter and record producer who built a career behind a metal mask and a supervillain persona. His dense, unhurried wordplay, stuffed with internal rhyme and comic-book asides, made him the defining figure of 2000s underground and alternative hip hop. 'Doomsday', from 1999's 'Operation: Doomsday', introduced the character; five years later the Madvillain album made with Madlib produced 'Accordion', a scrap of pump-organ menace that has outlived most of the decade's hits. 'Rapp Snitch Knishes', cut with Mr. Fantastik for 'MM..FOOD', showed the same gift for turning a groan-worthy pun into a genuine threat. A peer of Mos Def and El-P, he shaped the underground that followed, Joey Bada$$ among its heirs. He died in 2020, his standing as a lyricist still growing.

madlib.blurb: Crate-digging producer of endless dusty loops.
madlib.bio: Madlib, born in 1973, is an American DJ, producer and rapper whose eclectic, sample-heavy work has made him one of the most influential beatmakers in modern hip hop. He digs deep and wide, pulling loops from soul, jazz and obscure records and leaving the dust audible, and he rarely stays in one guise for long. The 2004 Madvillain album with MF DOOM is the best-known result: 'Accordion', 'All Caps' and 'Raid' are short, strange, perfectly weighted productions that gave DOOM his greatest canvas. He also worked with J Dilla, one of his most frequent collaborators, alongside Erykah Badu, Talib Kweli and Freddie Gibbs. Earl Sweatshirt and Blu both count him a formative influence. Prolific to the point of myth, Madlib treats production as an act of listening first and arranging second.

swizzbeatz.blurb: Ruff Ryders producer of stomping, stripped beats.
swizzbeatz.bio: Swizz Beatz, born in the Bronx in 1978, is an American producer, rapper and DJ who started out behind the decks in 1994 and was recognised across the industry by eighteen, working through his family's label Ruff Ryders Entertainment. His partnership with the label's flagship artist, the Yonkers rapper DMX, defined both careers: he was DMX's hype man, his DJ and his producer, and built the stark keyboard beats behind Ruff Ryders' Anthem in 1998 and 'Party Up (Up in Here)' in 2000. Those records made him one of East Coast hip hop's most visible figures while barely out of his teens, and their brute simplicity, a riff and a chant over drums like a slammed door, became one of the era's most copied templates. He stepped out as a performer too, on 'Money in the Bank' in 2007.

justblaze.blurb: Roc-A-Fella beatmaker of soaring soul samples.
justblaze.bio: Just Blaze, born in Paterson, New Jersey in 1978, is an American record producer who left Rutgers after three years to chase music and became the in-house architect at Roc-A-Fella Records through the early 2000s. There he developed the sped-up sampling style known as chipmunk soul, prominent across hip hop at the time, and pushed it towards the triumphant, stacking horns and drums until a track sounded like a stadium entrance. He produced 'Oh Boy' for Cam'ron in 2002, gave Jay-Z the marching 'Public Service Announcement (Interlude)' the following year, and built 'Touch the Sky' for his peer Kanye West in 2005. His run of Jay-Z productions helped define the label's imperial period. Even now a Just Blaze beat announces itself well before the first verse arrives.

kendrick.bio: Kendrick Lamar, born in 1987, is an American MC whose introspective, politically charged writing has made him one of the most acclaimed rappers of his generation. A West Coast writer to the core, he came up through Top Dawg Entertainment alongside Schoolboy Q before Dr. Dre signed him, a lineage running back through 2Pac and forward into almost everything since. 'Money Trees', cut with Jay Rock in 2012, showed the storytelling; 'Alright', from 'To Pimp a Butterfly', became a protest chant in 2015; 'HUMBLE.' took him to number one in 2017. The following year the Pulitzer Prize for Music went to him, a first for any musician working outside classical and jazz. He has recorded with J. Cole and Rapsody and kept Doechii close, while his long feud with Drake became the most watched rivalry in rap. Little Simz counts him an influence.

drake.blurb: Canadian hitmaker who fused rapping and singing.
drake.bio: Drake, born in 1986, is a Canadian MC and singer who spent the streaming era as pop music's centre of gravity. Lil Wayne mentored him and brought him to Cash Money Records, and from that base he blurred the line between rapping and singing until the distinction stopped mattering: 'Hotline Bling' in 2015, 'One Dance' with Wizkid and Kyla the following year, and the number one 'God's Plan' in 2018. He has recorded with Future, J. Cole, 21 Savage and Lil Baby, and shared a crew with Nicki Minaj. He has also been rap's most reliable antagonist, trading rounds with Pusha T and Meek Mill and, above all, with Kendrick Lamar, a long-running feud that spilled into a sequence of diss records and became the most closely followed rivalry in modern hip hop.

jcole.blurb: Fayetteville everyman with a producer's ear.
jcole.bio: J. Cole, born in 1985 on a German military base and raised in Fayetteville, North Carolina, is an American MC and record producer who made plainspoken self-examination a commercial force. The 2007 mixtape 'The Come Up' drew early attention, and after moving to New York for college Jay-Z's Roc Nation signed him in 2009; 'The Warm Up' and 'Friday Night Lights' followed and widened his audience considerably. 'Work Out' launched his debut album in 2011, but it was '2014 Forest Hills Drive' and its 'No Role Modelz' that made him a fixture, with the standalone 'Middle Child' arriving in 2019. He produces much of his own work, carrying a lineage from Nas and a mentorship from Jay-Z. Collaborations with Kendrick Lamar and Drake placed him at the centre of the decade's long argument about who was best.

nickiminaj.blurb: Queen of Rap with a hundred voices.
nickiminaj.bio: Nicki Minaj, born in 1982, is a rapper, singer and songwriter from Trinidad and Tobago, widely called the Queen of Rap and credited with driving female rap back into the mainstream from the 2010s onward. Lil Wayne mentored her, and alongside Drake she formed part of the crew that dominated the decade. Her gift is elasticity: a flow that switches accent, pitch and character mid-bar, given shape by a cast of alter egos. 'Super Bass' broke her wide open in 2011, 'Starships' pushed her fully into pop the following year, and 'Anaconda' made a spectacle of her in 2014. She has traded very public feuds with Lil' Kim, Remy Ma and Cardi B, recorded with Stefflon Don and stands as a peer to Young M.A. Lil Nas X and Doechii both count her an influence.

bigsean.blurb: Michigan MC signed by Kanye as a teenager.
bigsean.bio: Big Sean, born in 1988, is an American MC from Michigan who first met Kanye West while still a teenager and turned that encounter into a career, signing to West's GOOD Music in 2007. Mixtapes followed, and 'Finally Famous Vol. 3: Big' in 2010 built enough momentum that his debut album 'Finally Famous' reached number three on the Billboard 200 the next year. 'Hall of Fame' matched that peak in 2013, and between them the two records produced 'My Last', 'Marvin & Chardonnay', 'Dance (A$$)' and 'Beware'. His 2014 collaboration with E-40 became his biggest hit, and 'Bounce Back' extended the run in 2016. Technically nimble and unfailingly quotable, he built a bridge between the melodic instincts of Midwest rap and the pop machinery of his label. West's patronage opened the door; the punchlines kept it open.

wizkhalifa.blurb: Pittsburgh rapper with two number-one hits.
wizkhalifa.bio: Wiz Khalifa, born in 1987 and raised in Pittsburgh, is an American rapper, singer-songwriter and entrepreneur who turned an easy-going persona into durable mainstream success. He signed to the local independent Rostrum Records for his 2006 debut 'Show and Prove', and a brief tie-up with Warner Bros. followed. The Eurodance-tinged 'Say Yeah' gave him a first minor hit on urban radio in 2008, reaching both the Hot Rap Songs and Rhythmic Top 40 charts, but it was 'Black and Yellow' that carried him to number one in 2010. 'Young, Wild & Free' with Snoop Dogg and Bruno Mars followed in 2011, and his duet with Charlie Puth, 'See You Again', returned him to the top in 2015 and became far and away his most recognisable song. He came up alongside Mac Miller, a fellow rapper, friend and frequent collaborator.

macmiller.blurb: Pittsburgh rapper who grew up in public.
macmiller.bio: Mac Miller, born in 1992, was an American MC and producer who started out in Pittsburgh's local scene at fifteen and spent the rest of a short life growing up in public. He signed to the independent Rostrum Records in 2010 and broke through with the mixtapes 'K.I.D.S.' and 'Best Day Ever', the breezy 'Donald Trump' making him a fixture of the blog era in 2011. That same year 'Blue Slide Park' topped the Billboard 200, the first independently released debut to manage it since 1995. What followed was a steady deepening, and by 'Swimming' and its 'Self Care' in 2018 he was writing with unguarded honesty about addiction and repair. He died that year, with 'Circles' and its 'Good News' released posthumously. He recorded often with Wiz Khalifa and stood as a peer to Tyler, the Creator.

asaprocky.blurb: Harlem stylist who mainstreamed cloud rap.
asaprocky.bio: A$AP Rocky, born in 1988 and raised in Harlem, is an American rapper, producer, model and fashion designer who began as a member of the A$AP Mob collective and took his name from it. 'Peso' leaked online in the summer of 2011 and was on the radio within weeks, pulling the hazy, weightless sound then called cloud rap into mainstream attention, and 'Purple Swag' cemented the mood. He signed to Polo Grounds Music through RCA that October and released the mixtape 'Live. Love. A$AP' to wide critical acclaim. The following year he assembled Drake, Kendrick Lamar and 2 Chainz on a single posse cut, one of the era's defining star summits. A collaborator of Tyler, the Creator, he has always treated rap as a matter of style, image and texture as much as sound.

tyler.blurb: Odd Future ringleader turned lush pop auteur.
tyler.bio: Tyler, the Creator, born in 1991, is an American MC, producer and fashion designer whose career has been one long argument against being pinned down. He came up in the collective Odd Future, and the 2011 breakout 'Yonkers', raw and deliberately ugly, made him notorious before he was famous. Over the following decade the shock receded and the musicianship took over: 'See You Again', cut with Kali Uchis for 'Flower Boy' in 2017, and 'EARFQUAKE' from 'Igor' in 2019, his biggest chart success, trade menace for lush chords and open feeling. He produces his own records and uses alter egos as a structural device, drawing a clear line back to Pharrell Williams. Earl Sweatshirt is his closest crewmate, A$AP Rocky a frequent collaborator, and Mac Miller was a peer of the same generation.

oddfuture.blurb: LA collective that upended blog-era rap.
oddfuture.bio: Odd Future Wolf Gang Kill Them All, abbreviated to Odd Future or OFWGKTA, formed in Los Angeles in 2007 as an American alternative hip hop collective. More a teenage art gang than a group, it gathered rappers and producers alongside skateboarders, actors, film-makers and clothing designers, with Tyler, the Creator at its centre and Hodgy, Casey Veggies, Left Brain, Matt Martians, Jasper Dolphin, Taco Bennett and Syd in the original line-up. Domo Genesis, Mike G, Earl Sweatshirt and Frank Ocean were among those who joined later. Its members made deliberately abrasive, horrorcore-tinged music, ran their own visual and clothing worlds, and spread through the internet rather than radio. 'Oldie', the full-crew posse cut from 'The OF Tape Vol. 2' in 2012, gives nearly every member a verse, and 'Rella' catches the same moment. The careers that spun out of it reshaped alternative rap and R&B.

earlsweatshirt.blurb: Dense, downcast lyricist of the West Coast underground.
earlsweatshirt.bio: Earl Sweatshirt, born in 1994, is an American rapper and producer who started out in 2008 under the name Sly Tendencies, changing it when Tyler, the Creator brought him into Odd Future the following year. 'Earl', released in 2010 while he was still a teenager, was a display of vertiginous technical rapping that made him the collective's most gifted writer almost by acclamation. He returned with 'Chum' in 2012, trading shock for something quieter and sadder, and by 'Grief' in 2015 had arrived at the murky, drum-heavy, interior style that has defined him since. His father was the South African poet Keorapetse Kgositsile, a political writer. Madlib is his clearest influence, in the dust and the loops as much as the attitude, and he has recorded with Vince Staples. He remains close to the crew that raised him.

chancetherapper.bio: Chance the Rapper, born in 1993, is an American rapper, singer, producer and activist who made independence itself part of the art. His second mixtape 'Acid Rap', released in 2013, established him as the leading voice of a new Chicago generation and as proof that an unsigned artist could reach a national audience; 'Cocoa Butter Kisses' remains its warmest moment. 'Angels', cut with Saba in 2015, is a hometown celebration, and 'No Problem', made with Lil Wayne and 2 Chainz in 2016, won a Grammy and carried his refusal to sign with a label to the widest possible audience. He has worked with Kanye West, stands as a peer to Common and came up in the same Chicago circle as Noname. Buoyant where many of his peers were bleak, he made joy sound like a serious artistic position.

runthejewels.blurb: Duo trading verses over abrasive, political beats.
runthejewels.bio: Run the Jewels are an American hip hop duo formed in 2013 by the Brooklyn rapper and producer El-P and the Atlanta rapper Killer Mike, two veterans who found in each other a late-career second wind. Their self-titled debut was given away as a free download that year, and the three albums that followed, 'Run the Jewels 2' in 2014, 'Run the Jewels 3' in 2016 and 'RTJ4' in 2020, were released the same way, each meeting wide critical acclaim. The formula is simple and relentless: El-P's abrasive, industrial-leaning production beneath two voices trading bars line for line, comic bravado giving way to genuine political fury. The 2014 track recorded with Zack de la Rocha set the tone, and 'Legend Has It' in 2016 and 'Ooh LA LA' in 2020 show the partnership at full stride.

killermike.blurb: Southern rapper with a preacher's political force.
killermike.bio: Killer Mike, born Michael Render in 1975, is an American rapper, actor and activist whose delivery carries the force of a Sunday sermon. He arrived through OutKast, debuting on their album 'Stankonia' and appearing on the Grammy-winning single 'The Whole World', then signing to Big Boi's Purple Ribbon label, which mentored him toward the acclaimed solo debut 'Monster' in 2003. Independent records followed before he found his sharpest form on 'R.A.P. Music', home to the searing 'Reagan' and the swaggering 'Big Beast' with Bun B and T.I., both from 2012. Around the same time he became one half of Run the Jewels, among the most combustible duos of the era. On 'Michael' in 2023 he returned to his given name, with 'Run' featuring Young Thug. Political rap rarely sounds this alive, or this funny.

elp.blurb: Definitive Jux architect of dystopian underground rap.
elp.bio: El-P, born Jaime Meline in 1975, is an American producer and MC who built one of underground hip hop's most distinctive sounds, dense and clanging and cinematic. He first surfaced with Company Flow and became a driving force in alternative rap from the 1990s onward, above all as co-founder and boss of the Definitive Jux label, while producing records for the likes of Aesop Rock, Cage and Mr. Lif. His own 'Fantastic Damage' remains a landmark, its 'Deep Space 9mm' and 'Stepfather Factory' turning science-fiction paranoia into rhythm in 2002. A decade later 'The Full Retard' announced 'Cancer 4 Cure', and the years since have belonged to the duo Run the Jewels. A peer of MF DOOM and a collaborator of Danny Brown, he is the underground's great systems builder.

schoolboyq.blurb: West Coast menace with a melodic streak.
schoolboyq.bio: Schoolboy Q, born Quincy Hanley in 1986, is an American MC whose West Coast rap swings between hard-eyed street reporting and something looser and more melodic. He started recording in 2007, building a local reputation on early mixtapes before signing to Top Dawg Entertainment, the Carson label that also housed his crewmate Kendrick Lamar. Two well-received albums, 'Setbacks' in 2011 and 'Habits & Contradictions' the following year, established him as a critical favourite. He broke wide with 'Oxymoron', whose 'Man of the Year' arrived in 2014, while 'Collard Greens' had paired him with Lamar the year before. 'Studio', cut with BJ the Chicago Kid in 2014, showed the softer, soul-leaning side of his register. Within TDE's tight circle he is the rough-voiced counterweight, a rapper who can make menace sound almost playful.

tde.blurb: Carson label that built modern West Coast rap.
tde.bio: Top Dawg Entertainment is an American independent record label, founded in 2004 by the producer and executive Anthony Tiffith, known as Top Dawg, and based in Carson, California. Specialising in hip hop and R&B, it became the most consequential West Coast institution of its generation by signing young local talent and giving it room to develop. Kendrick Lamar is the flagship: 'm.A.A.d city' in 2012 and 'HUMBLE.' in 2017 read as much like label statements as personal ones. Schoolboy Q came up alongside him, and their 'Collard Greens' from 2013 captures the roster's easy chemistry. The label has since signed Doechii, extending its reach into a new decade. Run as a family business, with Tiffith's sons among the executives alongside label president Terrence Punch Henderson, TDE proved an independent could shape the mainstream rather than chase it.

future.blurb: Auto-Tuned architect of modern trap melancholy.
future.bio: Future, born Nayvadius Cash in 1983, is an American rapper, singer and producer who did more than anyone to make Auto-Tune an instrument of feeling rather than a gimmick. Mentored early by Gucci Mane and shaped by the long shadow of OutKast, he turned a slurred, melodic delivery into a whole grammar for trap. 'Turn On the Lights' in 2012 showed the tenderness beneath the haze, 'Jumpman' with Drake in 2015 showed the ruthless efficiency, and 'Mask Off' in 2017 gave the decade one of its indelible hooks. His long partnership with the producer Metro Boomin defined the sound of an era, and his collaborations with Young Thug pushed it further out. The strain of melodic pain he perfected runs straight through Roddy Ricch and Juice WRLD. Few rappers of his generation have shaped so much of what followed.

youngthug.blurb: Elastic voice that rewired rap's rulebook.
youngthug.bio: Young Thug, born Jeffery Williams in 1991, is an American rapper and singer whose elastic, unpredictable voice reset what a rap vocal could do. He began releasing mixtapes in 2011 and signed with 1017 Records, run by the Atlanta rapper Gucci Mane, where '1017 Thug' in 2013 announced a genuine original: yelps, croons, sudden bursts of clarity, all worn with equally unconventional style. 'Lifestyle', the 2014 Rich Gang single, made him a star, followed by 'Best Friend' in 2015 and 'Pick Up the Phone' with Travis Scott the year after. Drawing on Lil Wayne's freewheeling example, he passed the lesson on, mentoring Gunna and Lil Baby, working repeatedly with Future and Lil Durk, and leaving his fingerprints all over Lil Uzi Vert. Few voices of the era were imitated more, and none were harder to imitate well.

migos.blurb: Atlanta trio who reset rap's rhythmic clock.
migos.bio: Migos were an American hip hop group formed in Lawrenceville, Georgia, in 2008, built around Quavo, his nephew Takeoff, and their friend Offset. Their triplet flow, three voices trading and stacking syllables at speed, became the default rhythm of 2010s rap and seeped outward into pop and everyday speech. 'Versace' in 2013 was the breakthrough, 'Bad and Boujee' with Lil Uzi Vert made them inescapable in 2016, and 'T-Shirt' the following year proved they could build atmosphere as well as momentum. They came up under the mentorship of Gucci Mane and the management of Coach K, and worked with producers including Mike Will Made-It, Zaytoven, Murda Beatz, DJ Durel and Buddah Bless. Takeoff's death closed the story, but the group's rhythmic template remains one of the era's most widely borrowed inventions.

2chainz.blurb: Punchline king of the southern trap boom.
2chainz.bio: 2 Chainz, born Tauheed Epps in 1977, is an American rapper, songwriter and sometime actor with one of the most quotable pens in southern rap. Raised in College Park, Georgia, he first found an audience as one half of the duo Playaz Circle alongside Dolla Boy, signed to Ludacris's Disturbing tha Peace, where their 2007 single 'Duffle Bag Boy' broke through. Reinventing himself under a new name, he had a remarkable 2012: 'No Lie' with Drake, the strutting 'I'm Different' and 'Birthday Song' with Kanye West made him the most in-demand guest of the trap boom. His appeal is all in the timing, a deadpan drawl that lands absurd one-liners as though reading out a shopping list. Two decades in, he remains a fixture, as much a personality and businessman as an MC.

travisscott.blurb: Psychedelic trap maximalist and stadium showman.
travisscott.bio: Travis Scott, born Jacques Webster in 1991, is an American rapper, singer and producer who treats a record as an environment to get lost in rather than a set of verses. Mentored by Kanye West and shaped by Kid Cudi's melodic drift, he built a sound of layered vocals, sudden beat switches and cavernous space. 'Antidote' in 2015 was the first mass breakthrough, 'Goosebumps' with Kendrick Lamar followed in 2016, and 'SICKO MODE' in 2018 became a defining hit of the streaming decade, restless enough to feel like three songs at once. He has worked repeatedly with the producer Metro Boomin. With five number-one singles on the Hot 100, a Latin Grammy and a long list of nominations behind him, he is best understood live, where the records turn into something closer to a controlled riot.

21savage.blurb: Deadpan menace over Metro Boomin's darkness.
21savage.bio: 21 Savage, born Sheyaa Bin Abraham-Joseph in 1992, is a British-born rapper raised in the United States and based in Atlanta. His delivery is the opposite of theatrical, flat and unhurried and quiet, which is exactly what makes it frightening. After three independent mixtapes he found his defining partner in the producer Metro Boomin, whose cavernous, minor-key beats framed the 2016 EP 'Savage Mode' and its single 'X' with Future. 'Bank Account' carried him further into the mainstream in 2017, the year he signed to Epic Records, and 'a lot' with J. Cole in 2018 revealed a reflective, autobiographical streak beneath the coldness. He has also recorded with Drake. Few rappers have done more with less volume; the space around his voice does as much work as the words inside it.

meekmill.blurb: Philadelphia battle rapper turned motivational roar.
meekmill.bio: Meek Mill, born Robert Williams in 1987, is an American rapper from Philadelphia whose voice arrives at full volume and rarely drops below it. He learned his craft as a battle rapper and in the short-lived group the Bloodhoundz, signed briefly to T.I.'s Grand Hustle without releasing anything, then found his home in 2011 with Rick Ross's Maybach Music Group. Appearances on the label's 'Self Made Vol. 1' put him in front of a national audience, and 'Ima Boss' became his first entry on the Hot 100. 'Dreams and Nightmares (Intro)' from 2012 remains his signature, a slow, wounded opening that detonates halfway through into one of rap's great adrenaline surges. A long and public feud with Drake shadowed the years that followed, though by 2018 the two were trading verses on 'Going Bad'. He is hip hop's great striver.

metroboomin.blurb: Dark cinematic architect of trap's golden decade.
metroboomin.bio: Metro Boomin, born Leland Wayne in 1993, is an American record producer whose dark, cinematic beats became the default backdrop of the decade's rap. His signature is built from ominous minor-key melodies, cavernous low end and dramatic pauses that leave a rapper's voice hanging in empty air. The partnership with Future is the central one, yielding 'Mask Off' in 2017, while his work with 21 Savage, whom he has both produced and run with, gave that rapper his defining frame. He produced 'Bad and Boujee' for Migos in 2016, the year trap conquered pop, and has worked with Travis Scott, Young Thug, Gucci Mane, Kanye West, the Weeknd and Drake. 'Creepin', with the Weeknd and 21 Savage in 2022, applied the same instincts to widescreen R&B. Producers rarely become this recognisable from the first bar.

mikewillmadeit.blurb: Trap producer who colonised the pop charts.
mikewillmadeit.bio: Mike Will Made-It, born Michael Williams in 1989, is an American record producer who carried trap drums out of southern rap and into the centre of pop. His beats rest on hard, skittering hi-hats and simple, sticky melodic hooks, a formula flexible enough to serve almost anyone: 'No Lie' for 2 Chainz, 'Pop That' for French Montana in 2012, 'Bandz a Make Her Dance' for Juicy J, 'Pour It Up' for Rihanna, 'We Can't Stop' for Miley Cyrus and 'Humble' for Kendrick Lamar. 'Black Beatles' with Rae Sremmurd became inescapable in 2016, the same year he produced 'Formation' for Beyonce. He has also worked with Migos and Kanye West, and stepped out under his own name from 2013 with singles including '23'. Few producers move so easily between the club, the trap and the stadium.

childishgambino.blurb: Polymath rapper, singer and screen storyteller.
childishgambino.bio: Childish Gambino is the musical name of Donald Glover, born in 1983, an American rapper, singer, comedian, writer and filmmaker who has refused to be only one of those things. Hired to write for '30 Rock' at twenty-three and later familiar to millions as an actor on 'Community', he built a parallel career in music that grew steadily stranger and better. '3005' in 2013 caught the jittery, self-questioning voice of his early rapping, 'Redbone' in 2016 abandoned rap almost entirely for slow-burning falsetto soul, and 'This Is America' in 2018 fused the two into a piece of pop provocation that played like a national argument. He created and starred in the FX series 'Atlanta', winning Emmy and Golden Globe awards. Kid Cudi's example runs through it all: the same blurring of rap and song, the same openness.

cardib.blurb: New York voice that reopened rap for women.
cardib.bio: Cardi B, born Belcalis Almanzar in 1992, is an American rapper from New York City whose blunt, high-volume charisma made her one of the defining pop stars of her decade. She launched her music career in 2016, and two mixtapes later 'Bodak Yellow' turned her into a phenomenon in 2017. 'I Like It' brought Bad Bunny and J Balvin into her orbit in 2018, and 'WAP' with Megan Thee Stallion became the loudest pop event of 2020, gleefully unbothered by the outrage it caused. A long rivalry with Nicki Minaj played out in public, while newer voices such as GloRilla have since joined her on record. More than anything she is credited with restoring women rappers to the centre of popular music, where the writing turns out to be every bit as sharp as the volume.

liluzivert.blurb: Philadelphia shapeshifter who made rap sound emo.
liluzivert.bio: Lil Uzi Vert, born Symere Woods in 1995, is an American rapper and singer from Philadelphia whose music sits where rap, emo and pop collapse into one another. They broke through with the 2015 mixtape 'Luv Is Rage', which led to a deal with Atlantic through DJ Drama's Generation Now imprint, and 'Money Longer' in 2016 gave the weightless, melodic style its first hit. 'XO Tour Llif3' in 2017 was the moment the whole idea landed, a bleak, catchy, oddly euphoric record that spoke directly to a generation raised on playlists rather than genres, while 'The Way Life Goes' from the same year showed the sweeter side. Young Thug's vocal freedom and Chief Keef's blunt force are both audible here, and the collaborations with Juice WRLD sealed the emo-rap moment. The fashion is as restless as the music.

vincestaples.blurb: Deadpan West Coast realist and sharp observer.
vincestaples.bio: Vince Staples, born in 1993, is an American rapper whose flat, unsentimental delivery and dry humour make him one of rap's sharpest observers. He first appeared on records from the Odd Future orbit, notably Earl Sweatshirt's 'Earl' and 'Doris', and released the collaborative mixtape 'Stolen Youth' with Mac Miller after signing to Talib Kweli's Blacksmith label. A move to No I.D.'s ARTium imprint brought the acclaimed EP 'Hell Can Wait' in 2014 and its 'Blue Suede'. 'Norf Norf', from 'Summertime 06' in 2015, reported on his neighbourhood without romance or apology, and 'Big Fish' in 2017 set the same voice against restless, club-facing production. He works inside the conventions of West Coast gangsta rap while refusing its myths, describing violence as tedium rather than glamour. He is the era's great deadpan narrator.

joeybadass.blurb: Brooklyn revivalist of nineties boom bap.
joeybadass.bio: Joey Bada$$, born Jo-Vaughn Scott in 1995, is an American rapper from Brooklyn who arrived as a teenager sounding as though he had been raised entirely on nineties New York rap. He formed the group Pro Era in 2011 and the wider Beast Coast collective the following year; 'Survival Tactics', cut with his friend Capital STEEZ in 2012, announced both a technically dazzling MC and a scene. The debts to Nas and MF DOOM are worn openly, in the dense internal rhyme and the taste for dusty, sample-driven beats. 'Devastated' in 2016 reached for something broader and more anthemic, and 'Land of the Free' the year after turned his gaze on the country around him. For younger New York rappers such as Kota the Friend, he is proof that the old blueprint still works.

dannybrown.blurb: Cackling yelp over gloriously unhinged production.
dannybrown.bio: Danny Brown, born Daniel Sewell in 1981, is an American rapper, songwriter and podcaster with one of the most immediately identifiable voices in the music, a high, cackling yelp that can flip into a low deadpan mid-line. His records match it, pairing alternative and psychedelic production with writing that swings between party abandon and bleak self-examination. 'Grown Up' in 2012 was the charming, nostalgic side; 'Dip', from 'Old' in 2013, went straight for the rave; and 'Ain't It Funny', from 'Atrocity Exhibition' in 2016, turned dread into a lurching, blackly comic showpiece. He has collaborated with El-P, a fellow traveller in abrasive and uncompromising rap. Brown belongs to no camp in particular, which is a large part of why he has quietly become one of the most admired MCs of his generation.

chiefkeef.bio: Chief Keef, born Keith Cozart in 1995, is an American rapper and producer who was still a teenager when he changed the direction of hip hop. He built a regional following on mixtapes in the early 2010s, then broke out with 'I Don't Like', made with Lil Reese, and 'Love Sosa', both from 2012: menacing, minimal, repetitive in the way a chant is repetitive, and delivered with a bored authority nobody could imitate. Kanye West took notice and worked with him, carrying the sound to a national audience, and 'Faneto' in 2014 became an enduring anthem. As drill's progenitor his influence is enormous and easy to trace, through Lil Durk and King Von in Chicago, through Pop Smoke's Brooklyn variant, and through the melodic reinventions of Lil Uzi Vert. Few artists so young have reshaped so much.

lilbaby.blurb: Georgia's conversational voice of the streaming decade.
lilbaby.bio: Lil Baby, born Dominique Jones in 1994, is an American rapper whose casual, conversational flow disguises how much craft goes into it. Mentored by Young Thug, he moved fast once he started: the 2017 mixtapes 'Harder than Hard' and 'Too Hard' brought his first chart entry with 'My Dawg', and a deal with Quality Control led to 'Harder Than Ever' in 2018, home to 'Yes Indeed' with Drake. Later that year the joint tape 'Drip Harder', made with his running mate Gunna, gave both of them a signature in 'Drip Too Hard', while 'Street Gossip' reached number two on the album chart. 'The Bigger Picture' in 2020 turned that easy voice toward something graver and more public. He makes difficulty sound effortless, which is the hardest trick in modern rap.

roddyricch.blurb: Compton singer-rapper of the melodic trap wave.
roddyricch.bio: Roddy Ricch, born Rodrick Moore in 1998, is an American rapper and singer from Compton, California, who arrived with a voice that slides from rapping into full song without a seam. Two acclaimed mixtapes, 'Feed Tha Streets' and its sequel, preceded his rise in 2018 with 'Die Young', written as a tribute to rappers who had died young. The following year he guested on Nipsey Hussle's 'Racks in the Middle', which won a Grammy for Best Rap Performance, and on Mustard's 'Ballin', another nominee and a top-fifteen hit. Then came 'The Box', the opening statement of 'Please Excuse Me for Being Antisocial' in 2019, whose squeaking hook became one of the most recognisable sounds of the streaming era. The melodic ache he inherited from Future runs through everything he sings.

meganthestallion.blurb: Viral freestyler turned unstoppable hot girl.
meganthestallion.bio: Megan Thee Stallion, born Megan Pete in 1995, is an American rapper, songwriter and screen actress who built her reputation the hard way, on freestyles that went viral and proved she could out-rap almost anyone put in front of her. Signed in 2018, she broke through with the mixtape 'Fever' in 2019 and the EP 'Suga' the following year, both reaching the top ten of the album chart. 'Hot Girl Summer', with Nicki Minaj and Ty Dolla Sign, turned a catchphrase into a season in 2019; 'Savage' in 2020 became a dance craze and then something bigger; and 'Body' from the same year was pure muscular showmanship. Her collaboration with Cardi B produced one of the loudest pop moments of the era. The drawl and the swagger owe a clear debt to Pimp C, whose example she has never hidden.

popsmoke.bio: Pop Smoke, born Bashar Jackson, was an American rapper from Brooklyn whose growling baritone gave New York a new sound almost overnight. Building on the Chicago drill of Chief Keef but working with British drill producers, whose beats ran sparser and more aggressive, he brought the style home as Brooklyn drill. 'Welcome to the Party' in 2019 was the arrival, an instant city anthem, and 'Dior' the same year proved he could carry melody as well as menace. He was mentored by 50 Cent, ran with Fivio Foreign, stood alongside Young M.A in a resurgent New York scene, and shared the transatlantic drill current with Headie One. His death in 2020 came before he could see what he had started; 'For the Night', with Lil Baby and DaBaby, arrived that year. The blueprint outlived him.

juicewrld.blurb: Emo rap's most gifted melodic confessor.
juicewrld.bio: Juice WRLD, born Jarad Higgins in 1998, was an American rapper and singer who became the leading voice of emo rap, a style that traded bravado for heartbreak, anxiety and self-medication and dominated the streaming charts in the late 2010s. He took his name from the 1992 film 'Juice', explaining that it meant taking over the world, and for a short time he very nearly did. 'All Girls Are the Same' and 'Lucid Dreams', both from 2018, made grief sound like pop, sung in a soft, bruised melody thousands of teenagers already knew by heart, and 'Robbery' followed in 2019. The melodic openness he learned from Future ran through all of it, alongside a real debt to rock. He collaborated with Lil Uzi Vert, his closest peer, before his death in 2019 cut the story short.

lildurk.blurb: Chicago drill's most durable melodic survivor.
lildurk.bio: Lil Durk, born Durk Banks in 1992, is an American rapper who helped pioneer Chicago drill and became, in time, its most commercially successful figure. He came up alongside Chief Keef in the scene's first wave, and his 'Signed to the Streets' mixtapes led to a deal with Def Jam and the albums 'Remember My Name' in 2015 and 'Lil Durk 2X' the following year. The label let him go in 2018, which turned out to be the making of him: he rebuilt around a sung, wounded delivery that suited grief better than aggression. 'Laugh Now Cry Later' with Drake took him to the top in 2020, 'Backdoor' followed in 2021, and 'All My Life' with J. Cole confirmed his reach in 2023. He has worked with Young Thug and Polo G, and ran with King Von.

polog.blurb: Melodic drill storyteller in the 2Pac lineage.
polog.bio: Polo G, born Taurus Bartlett in 1999, is an American rapper and singer whose melodic drill is built around storytelling and a strain of hard-won reflection. 'Finer Things' and 'Pop Out', the latter with Lil Tjay, made his name in 2019 and led to the debut album 'Die a Legend', which reached number six on the Billboard 200 and went double platinum, a feat his next two albums matched. 'Rapstar' gave him a number-one single in 2021. He has collaborated with Lil Durk, a fellow rapper working the same seam of drill turned inward, and he holds up 2Pac as his model, sharing the same instinct to pair street detail with conscience and to sing the hooks himself. Still young, he is among the most consistent hitmakers of his generation.

jackharlow.blurb: Easy-charm rapper of the streaming mainstream.
jackharlow.bio: Jack Harlow, born Jackman Harlow in 1998, is an American rapper and singer whose appeal rests on charm, timing and a conversational ease that owes much to Drake's example. He began recording in 2015 and released a run of EPs and mixtapes before signing in 2018 to Generation Now, the label run by DJ Drama and Don Cannon under Atlantic. 'What's Poppin' turned him into a star in 2020, its bounce and unhurried punchlines carrying it far beyond rap radio. The following year he stole a verse on Lil Nas X's 'INDUSTRY BABY', and in 2022 'First Class' gave him a self-assured pop hit of his own. He is a rapper built for the streaming age, light on his feet, quick with a hook and entirely comfortable in the mainstream.

gunna.blurb: Silk-voiced trap stylist of the drip era.
gunna.bio: Gunna, born Sergio Kitchens in 1993, is an American rapper, singer and producer whose smooth, unhurried delivery glides over trap production rather than attacking it. Mentored by Young Thug, he signed to his YSL label in 2016 and made his name with the mixtape 'Drip Season 3' in 2018, the year he and his running mate Lil Baby released the joint tape 'Drip Harder'. Its single 'Drip Too Hard' reached number four on the Hot 100, was certified diamond and earned a Grammy nomination, and the word drip became shorthand for a whole aesthetic. 'pushin P', made with Young Thug and Future in 2022, coined another, and 'fukumean' in 2023 was a hit built on the same effortless glide. Few rappers make luxury sound so relaxed, or turn slang into currency so quickly.

lilnasx.blurb: Country-rap disruptor who rewrote pop's rules.
lilnasx.bio: Lil Nas X, born Montero Hill in 1999, is an American rapper and singer-songwriter who turned internet fluency into one of the biggest pop careers of his era. 'Old Town Road', a country-rap novelty that refused to stay a novelty, spent a then-record nineteen weeks at number one on the Hot 100, a run that dragged questions about genre boundaries into public argument. While it sat there he came out publicly as gay: no artist before him had done that while holding the number-one record. He proved it was no fluke with 'MONTERO (Call Me by Your Name)' in 2021, a defiantly queer single wrapped in deliberate provocation, and 'INDUSTRY BABY' with Jack Harlow the same year. A longtime admirer of Nicki Minaj, he learned from her how a persona can be an instrument.

centralcee.blurb: Shepherd's Bush voice of UK drill.
centralcee.bio: Central Cee, born in London in 1998, is a rapper from Shepherd's Bush and one of the defining voices of UK drill. He broke through in 2020 with 'Loading', a single that carried the sound of west London into the national conversation, and consolidated it with the mixtape Wild West in 2021, which entered the UK albums chart at number two, and its follow-up 23 in 2022, which went to the top. The playful 'Doja' in 2022 widened his audience further, and in 2023 he joined Dave for 'Sprinter', pairing the two biggest names in British rap. He has also worked with Drake, and stands alongside peers such as Headie One in the generation that took drill out of the estates and into the charts. His delivery is conversational, unhurried and quietly precise.

stormzy.bio: Stormzy, born in London in 1993 to Ghanaian parents, is the rapper and singer who carried grime into the mainstream. He built his name in 2014 on the UK underground with the Wicked Skengman freestyles, riding classic grime beats with a bruising, unhurried authority. 'Shut Up', released in 2015 as a YouTube freestyle, took on a life of its own, reaching number eight in the UK singles chart once he mounted a campaign for the Christmas number one. 'Big for Your Boots' followed in 2017 and 'Vossi Bop' in 2019, by which point his reach extended far beyond the scene that raised him. A collaborator of Dave, he pairs street-level directness with gospel warmth and open political conviction. Stormzy remains the artist most often credited with proving that a grime MC could headline anywhere.

dave.blurb: Socially conscious lyricist of British rap.
dave.bio: Dave, born in London in 1998 and sometimes billed as Santan Dave, is a rapper, producer and actor known for socially conscious writing and dense wordplay. He arrived with the grime cut 'Thiago Silva' alongside AJ Tracey, and his debut EP Six Paths followed in 2016, the same year Drake premiered a remix of his song 'Wanna Know'. A second EP, Game Over, came in 2017, and in 2018 his political track 'Question Time' took the Ivor Novello Award for Best Contemporary Song. 'Funky Friday' with Fredo gave him his first UK number one that year, and 'Location' with Burna Boy followed in 2019. In 2023 he and Central Cee made 'Sprinter'. A collaborator of Stormzy and a peer of Little Simz, Dave writes at album length about class, race and family with unusual patience.

glorilla.blurb: Memphis rapper with a crunk roar.
glorilla.bio: GloRilla, born in Memphis in 1999, is a rapper whose hoarse, hollering delivery reconnected mainstream hip hop with the crunk and Memphis rap traditions she grew up inside. Her 2022 single 'F.N.F. (Let's Go)' became an immediate anthem, reaching the upper half of the Billboard Hot 100 and earning a Grammy nomination for Best Rap Performance. Its success led her to sign that July with Collective Music Group, the label run by fellow Memphis rapper Yo Gotti. 'Tomorrow 2' with Cardi B arrived later the same year, and 'Yeah Glo!' followed in 2024. She carries forward the line from Three 6 Mafia and from Gangsta Boo, whose blunt, unbothered swagger is audible in her cadences. GloRilla writes for the room rather than the radio, which is exactly why the radio came for her.

latto.blurb: Atlanta rapper who outgrew reality television.
latto.bio: Latto, born in Atlanta in 1998, is a rapper and singer who turned an early television win into a career on her own terms. She appeared on Jermaine Dupri's series The Rap Game in 2016 under the name Miss Mulatto and won the first season, then refused the label deal with Dupri's So So Def that came with it. She built an independent following instead, breaking through in 2019 with 'Bitch from da Souf', a southern anthem that established the brassy confidence of her delivery. 'Big Energy' in 2021 pushed her into pop territory without softening her, and 'Put It on da Floor Again' with Cardi B followed in 2023. She counts T.I. among the Atlanta figures who shaped her. Latto's writing is competitive and plainspoken, built for the club and the cypher alike.

nbayoungboy.blurb: Prolific, unfiltered voice of modern trap.
nbayoungboy.bio: YoungBoy Never Broke Again, born in 1999 and also billed as NBA YoungBoy, is a rapper and singer whose extraordinary output has made him one of the most streamed artists of his generation. He released eight mixtapes between 2015 and 2017 and built a regional following before signing to Atlantic Records and Artist Partner Group, which yielded 'Untouchable' in 2017, his first entry on the Billboard Hot 100. 'Outside Today' in 2018 was his mainstream breakthrough, reaching the chart's top forty and leading his debut album Until Death Call My Name, which peaked at number seven. 'Bandit' with Juice WRLD followed in 2019. He came up admiring Lil Wayne, and his long-running rivalry with Lil Durk has shadowed both careers. His songs are raw, melodic and delivered as though there were no time to revise them.

jazzyjeff.blurb: Turntable technician behind the Fresh Prince.
jazzyjeff.bio: DJ Jazzy Jeff, born Jeffrey Townes in 1965, is a DJ and record producer, one half of the duo DJ Jazzy Jeff and the Fresh Prince alongside Will Smith. Together they made 'Parents Just Don't Understand' in 1988, the sunlit 'Summertime' in 1991 and 'Boom! Shake the Room' in 1993, records that proved rap could be warm, funny and enormous all at once. He is credited alongside DJ Spinbad and DJ Cash Money with popularising the transformer scratch, a technique that became foundational vocabulary for the turntable. He learned from the example of Grandmaster Flash and stood among peers including Jam Master Jay, DJ Premier and Run-DMC. Behind the boards he has produced widely and mentored generations of DJs, and he has acted on screen. His hands remain among the most respected in the culture.

foxybrown.bio: Foxy Brown, born in New York in 1978, is a rapper whose luxurious, hard-edged writing helped define the sound of late-nineties East Coast hip hop. She signed to Def Jam and released her debut album Ill Na Na in 1996 to critical and commercial success, reaching number seven on the Billboard 200, going platinum in the United States and selling over seven million copies worldwide. It was carried by 'I'll Be' with Jay-Z, a Hot 100 top ten hit, while 'Get Me Home' with Blackstreet arrived the same year and 'Hot Spot' followed in 1998. She ran with Nas, collaborated repeatedly with Jay-Z, and her rivalry with Lil' Kim became one of the defining storylines of the era. Also a model and actor, Foxy Brown made unapologetic appetite a central subject of her records.

dabrat.blurb: First female solo rapper to go platinum.
dabrat.bio: Da Brat, born Shawntae Harris in Chicago in 1974, is a rapper whose easy, elastic flow carried her to a milestone no woman in hip hop had reached before. She began performing in 1992 and signed two years later to So So Def Recordings, Jermaine Dupri's label, releasing her debut album Funkdafied in 1994. It was certified platinum, making her the first female solo rap act to achieve that, and the title track and 'Give It 2 You' both landed the same year. 'What'chu Like' with Tyrese followed in 1999, a smoother, sung-hook turn that showed her range. She has collaborated with Missy Elliott and came up in the wake of Salt-N-Pepa, whose success made her own path thinkable. Also an actor on film and television, Da Brat rapped with a relaxed authority that never asked permission.

miax.blurb: Mother of No Limit, New Orleans matriarch.
miax.bio: Mia X, born in New Orleans in 1970, is a rapper and songwriter who came up through the city's early-nineties bounce scene before becoming the first female emcee signed to Master P's No Limit Records. She was central to the label's dominant run, appearing across the label's defining albums, Charge It 2 Da Game, Ghetto D and Ice Cream Man, alongside Master P and Silkk the Shocker. Her own records carried a maternal, battle-ready authority that set her apart in a roster built on aggression: 'Da Payback' arrived in 1995, and 'What'cha Wanna Do' with Charlie Wilson followed in 1998. A peer of Trina in the southern lineage of women who rapped on their own terms, she has long been known as the Mother of No Limit. Mia X made New Orleans phrasing legible to the rest of the country.

gangstaboo.blurb: Queen of Memphis, Three 6 Mafia's first lady.
gangstaboo.bio: Gangsta Boo, born Lola Mitchell in 1979, was a Memphis rapper who died in 2023, and who joined Three 6 Mafia at fourteen and became the group's fiercest and most quotable presence. She appeared on six of their albums, including 'Tear da Club Up '97' in 1997 and the Tear Da Club Up Thugs re-recording of 'Slob on My Knob' in 1999, and cut her own signature single 'Where Dem Dollas At' in 1998 with DJ Paul and Juicy J. She left the group and its label after Both Worlds *69, her second solo album, in 2001 over financial disputes and how the record was promoted, then built a long independent run, collaborating with Foxy Brown, La Chat, Eminem, Outkast, Run the Jewels, Lil Jon, Latto and GloRilla. Her voice runs straight through GloRilla's generation of Memphis rappers.

yoyo.blurb: West Coast MC who answered back.
yoyo.bio: Yo-Yo, born Yolanda Whitaker in 1971, is a South Los Angeles rapper and actress who brought a woman's rebuttal into the heart of West Coast hip hop. Ice Cube mentored her and put her on record early: their duet 'It's a Man's World' appeared on his 1990 album AmeriKKKa's Most Wanted, an argument staged as a song. Her own 'You Can't Play with My Yo-Yo' in 1991, featuring Cube, became her signature, and 'The Bonnie & Clyde Theme' followed in 1993 with him again. She also worked with MC Lyte, one of the few contemporaries writing from a comparable position of authority. Alongside the records she built an acting career on television and film. Yo-Yo's contribution was to make self-possession sound as tough as anything the era's men were saying.

monielove.blurb: British pioneer among golden age emcees.
monielove.bio: Monie Love, born Simone Johnson in London in 1970, is a rapper, actress and radio personality, and the first British woman to make a decisive mark on American hip hop. She ran with the Jungle Brothers and appeared on Queen Latifah's 'Ladies First' in 1989, a record that put two women's voices at the centre of a scene that rarely made room for one. Her own 'Monie in the Middle' and 'It's a Shame (My Sister)' both arrived in 1990, quick-tongued and buoyant, and she became a two-time Grammy nominee, the first British hip hop artist ever to do so. Latterly she has worked in radio, broadcasting for an urban adult contemporary station in Atlanta. Monie Love's rapid, bouncing delivery gave the golden age one of its most immediately recognisable voices.

trina.bio: Trina, born Katrina Kearse in 1978, is a Miami rapper, songwriter and music executive whose brazen writing set the template for a generation of southern women. She first drew attention through her verses on fellow Floridian Trick Daddy's records, beginning with 'Nann' in 1998, then signed to the Miami label Slip-N-Slide and released her debut album Da Baddest Bitch in 2000. It produced 'Pull Over', which put her on the Billboard Hot 100 as a lead artist for the first time and remains her calling card. Diamond Princess followed in 2002, reaching number fourteen and spawning 'B R Right', and 'Single Again' led Still da Baddest in 2007. She has recorded with Lil Wayne, Rick Ross and Missy Elliott, and stands as a peer of Mia X. Trina made luxury, sex and independence a single unbroken argument.

remyma.blurb: Bronx battle rapper of ferocious technique.
remyma.bio: Remy Ma, born Reminisce Smith in 1980, is a rapper whose technical ferocity has made her one of the most feared verse-writers in New York hip hop. She was discovered by Big Pun and came to prominence through Fat Joe's group Terror Squad, whose 'Lean Back' became a number one hit in 2004 and carried her voice to a mass audience. Her first solo record under her own name, There's Something About Remy: Based on a True Story, arrived in 2006 and sold thirty-seven thousand copies in its first week, yielding 'Conceited'. A decade later she reunited with Fat Joe for 'All the Way Up' in 2016, her biggest record since. Her prolonged feud with Nicki Minaj became one of the most closely watched rivalries of its moment. Remy Ma raps with the compressed aggression of a battle competitor who never left the ring.

rapsody.blurb: North Carolina lyricist in the Lauryn Hill line.
rapsody.bio: Rapsody, born Marlanna Evans in 1983, is a rapper whose dense, unhurried writing has made her a critical favourite and a rapper's rapper. She signed to the producer 9th Wonder's It's a Wonderful World Music Group, releasing a run of mixtapes and collaborating with Erykah Badu and Talib Kweli before her debut album The Idea of Beautiful in 2012. Wider recognition followed when Kendrick Lamar featured her on 'Complexion' from To Pimp a Butterfly in 2015; the two reunited for 'Power' in 2017 alongside Lance Skiiiwalker. 'Nina' and 'Sassy' arrived in 2019 as part of a body of work that names Black women as its subject and its dedication. She later signed with Jay-Z, and she writes in the tradition Lauryn Hill established. Rapsody puts craft ahead of spectacle and has never had to apologise for it.

youngma.blurb: Brooklyn rapper who broke through unbothered.
youngma.bio: Young M.A, born Katorah Marrero in 1992, is a rapper, entrepreneur and film director who arrived fully formed with one of the defining singles of 2016. 'OOOUUU' reached number sixteen on the Billboard Hot 100 and was certified quadruple platinum, while its video passed four hundred million views by 2019, all of it achieved without softening her delivery, her subject matter or her presentation. 'PettyWap' followed in 2018 and 'Big' in 2019, and her first album, Herstory in the Making, arrived that year, also reaching number sixteen and drawing positive reviews. She stands as a peer of Nicki Minaj and of the late Pop Smoke in the New York lineage that runs through her drawled, conversational flow. Young M.A made openly living as herself an unremarkable fact of a mainstream rap career.

noname.blurb: Chicago poet turned quietly radical rapper.
noname.bio: Noname, born Fatimah Warner in 1991, is a rapper whose soft, conversational delivery carries some of the most politically pointed writing of her generation. She started out in 2010 rapping and reading slam poetry, and reached a wider audience in 2013 through 'Lost', a track from Chance the Rapper's Acid Rap mixtape. Her debut mixtape Telefone followed in 2016 to considerable acclaim, carried by the warm, grief-shadowed 'Diddy Bop' with Raury and Cam O'bi and by 'Shadow Man'. Room 25 in 2018 sharpened both the jazz-inflected arrangements and the critique inside them, and the standalone 'Song 33' arrived in 2020. She came up in Chance the Rapper's circle and stands in a line with Common. Noname rarely raises her voice, which makes the things she says land harder.
